text: Welcome to the AutoCaller user guide. Here's how to set up two phones and start your calls.
You need two Android phones. Phone one calls your number list, with the call on speaker. Phone two listens, and when the person says hello, it plays your recorded message.
Step one. Install AutoCaller on phone one, and AutoCaller Player on phone two. If Android asks, allow installs from this source, then tap Install.
Step two. Open AutoCaller on phone one. In the Setup box, tap Set to make it the default phone app. Then allow the permissions and the battery setting, until all three lines turn green.
Step three. On phone two, open AutoCaller Player. Tap Record, speak your message clearly, and tap Stop. Note the length it shows, for example, twenty-eight seconds.
Here's AutoCaller Player on a real phone, with the message ready.

Step four. Add the numbers you want to call. On phone one, tap View or edit list, then Add numbers. Type one number on each line. You can add a name after a comma. Then tap Add. For a long list, tap Import CSV instead, and pick a file with names and mobile numbers.
Step five. Open Settings on phone one. Choose Second phone plays the message. Under Hang-up timer, enter the message length, keep five seconds after it, and tap Save.
And here's AutoCaller on the real phone, ready to call.
Step six. Place the two phones side by side, with phone two's speaker next to phone one's microphone. Tap Start listening on phone two. Then tap Start on phone one.
Here's a real test call. Listen.
When the run is done, open Reports. Every call is listed as answered, busy, or not reached, and you can save the report as a CSV file.
That's it. Set it up once, press Start, and let your phones do the calling.
